title: WRAP up your backlog with GitHub Copilot coding agent - The GitHub Blog

facts.fact: GitHub's engineers have been using GitHub Copilot coding agent for over a year, as stated in a blog post published 2025-12-26.
facts.quote: Engineers at GitHub have been using GitHub Copilot coding agent for over a year now, studying through experience where it can help save developers real time and energy.

facts.fact: The GitHub Blog post 'WRAP up your backlog with GitHub Copilot coding agent' was published on 2025-12-26.
GitHub's WRAP acronym for using Copilot coding agent stands for Write effective issues, Refine your instructions, Atomic tasks, and Pair with the coding agent.
Per GitHub's blog, custom agents for coding agent can be created with a natural language text file and apply at the enterprise, organization, or repository level.
facts.quote: are applicable at either the enterprise, organization, or repository level

facts.fact: GitHub states that a user can assign ten different tasks to coding agent at once and expect it to work on each of them.
facts.quote: You can assign ten different tasks to coding agent right now and expect it to work on each of them.

facts.fact: GitHub recommends breaking a large problem into multiple, independent, smaller tasks when assigning it to coding agent.
facts.quote: the trick is to break that large problem down into multiple, independent, smaller tasks.
